targets.title: Exposing individuals to foreign accent increases their trust in what nonnative speakers say
targets.evidence_quote:
We conducted a close replication and extension of the study reported in Boduch-Grabka and Lev-Ari (
Reference Boduch-Grabka and Lev-Ari
2021
).
targets.outcome_quote: In contrast to the original study, we did not find that British-English-speaking listeners judged statements produced by Polish-accented English speakers as less likely to be true than statements produced by British-accented English speakers. We also did not find an effect of prior exposure to Polish-accented English speech on veracity judgments, and no effect of exposure on comprehension of Polish-accented sentences. On the basis of these findings, we conclude that the previously observed accent-based reduction in veracity judgments for this populations of listeners, and this particular set of speech materials, may not be robust to replication.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Overall conclusion and individual comparisons report absence of the original accent and exposure effects. Compatibility with a processing-difficulty theory is not successful replication of the original empirical results.

reasoning: Completed preregistered new-sample close replication. Boduch-Grabka and Lev-Ari is the directly retested paper; earlier sources of the general accent claim are not additional targets in the chain. An original-data mean comparison is incidental to the new-sample replication. Publisher title and metadata authors match; article body and reference list extracted separately.
